title: Prefix-aware KV cache eviction with correctness guarantees
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: existing KV cache uses a simple global LRU with TTL. With continuous batching and variable prefix workloads (chat sessions, embeddings prefixes, instruction families) we see uneven memory pressure on GPUs and correctness edge cases during model rollouts and sharded execution. This ticket designs and implements a prefix-aware eviction policy that combines LRU, TTL, and prefix affinity scoring, and adds correctness guarantees across sharded KV caches and in-flight requests.
acceptance_criteria: Eviction policy supports LRU + TTL + prefix affinity scoring and is configurable per deployment (hosted/dedicated/private)
Eviction decisions are atomic w.r.t. in-flight decode steps: no request should use a partially-evicted KV entry leading to decoding corruption
Cache snapshots and eviction logs available in Console for a route/model to inspect per-prefix eviction events
Unit and integration tests cover race conditions: concurrent read/evict, eviction during checkpointing, and model rollback scenarios
End-to-end benchmark: tail-latency increase <= 5% under peak memory pressure compared to baseline but 20% fewer OOM-related fallbacks
Feature toggle and rollout gating in runtime-2.4; ability to revert to legacy LRU quickly
design_decisions: Eviction scoring: score = alpha * recency_score + beta * ttl_penalty + gamma * prefix_affinity_boost. alpha/beta/gamma configurable via runtime flags.
Prefix affinity: grouping keys by stable prefix hash (e.g., session_id, prompt template id) to avoid evicting hot prefixes prematurely.
Correctness: use versioned KV handles and a lightweight epoch counter to ensure readers see either the pre-eviction or post-eviction state, never a partial state.
Shard coordination: per-GPU local eviction decisions with periodic global reconciliation during low-load windows to rebalance per-prefix distribution.
Fallbacks: when eviction cannot free enough memory, automatically fallback to a lower-precision quantized kernel path or route to a capacity tier; this integrates with smart routing policy.
Telemetry: emit eviction_reason, evicted_prefix, freed_bytes, num_live_handles at INFO level and aggregate to Console metrics.
implementation_tasks: Add prefix extraction hooks in tokenizer/route layer to populate KV metadata (ENG-5824-1)
Implement epoched KV handle with atomic replace semantics in runtime core (ENG-5824-2)
Eviction scorer module + config flags; unit tests for score ordering (ENG-5824-3)
Per-shard reconcile worker that runs during quiet windows (ENG-5824-4)
Integrate eviction telemetry into Console ingestion pipeline (ENG-5824-5)
Create rolling upgrade plan and feature flag to enable prefix-aware eviction (ENG-5824-6)
End-to-end load test harness for memory pressure scenarios with continuous batching enabled (ENG-5824-7)
testing_plan: Unit tests: scorer correctness, TTL expiry, prefix grouping correctness
Concurrency tests: spawn readers/writers/evictors with randomized timing to surface races
Fault injection: simulate failed eviction halfway and assert readers either get old value or new value but never corrupted token stream
Integration: DRAM/GPU memory-pressure tests on CI cluster; validate automatic fallback triggers and routing behavior
Regression: compare generation outputs against baseline prompts after eviction events to ensure deterministic decoding for pinned requests
Load test: 48-hour soak with mixed prefixes, measure evictions/hour, OOM events, and tail latency
rollout_plan: Feature flag off in runtime Canary build; deploy to 2 non-critical regions
Enable prefix metadata collection only (no eviction) for 24 hours to verify prefix distribution metrics
Enable eviction with conservative gamma=0.25 and observe metrics for 48 hours
Gradually increase traffic exposure then tune alpha/beta/gamma per workload; roll back if OOMs or significant accuracy regressions observed
Post-mortem checkpoint and add to runbook: steps to force-evict, revert to LRU, and escalate
metrics_and_dashboards: Console: KV Eviction Rate by reason (LRU/TTL/prefix), per-route and per-model
Console: Freed GPU bytes per minute and live_kv_handles by prefix
Alert: sudden spike in eviction TTL_penalty > 80% or OOM fallback rate > 0.1%
Benchmark dashboard: tail P95/P99 latency comparison pre/post feature
Cost model: token-cost delta when using fallback routing or quantized kernels
references: Related ticket: ENG-5601 (KV shard rebalancer), ENG-5722 (batching backpressure)
